title: The birth of Spätlese
subtitle: A late messenger
objectives: Explain the role of noble rot

steps.title: The late messenger
steps.body: In 1775, the monks of Schloss Johannisberg needed permission from the Prince-Bishop of Fulda to start the harvest. The messenger returned weeks late. By then, the grapes had shrivelled with noble rot. The monks made wine anyway, and it was remarkable. That late harvest, Spätlese, became a recognised style.

steps.title: Noble rot
steps.body: The story shows the role of Botrytis cinerea: when grapes are left on the vine in misty autumn weather, noble rot concentrates sugar and acidity and adds honeyed aromas. From Spätlese came Auslese, selected bunches, and later Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese, picked berry by berry.

steps.prompt: Why was the 1775 harvest at Schloss Johannisberg late?
options: The messenger with permission arrived weeks late
steps.explanation: The delay let noble rot develop, creating Spätlese.

steps.title: Schloss Johannisberg
steps.body: Schloss Johannisberg sits on a hill above the Rhine, on the 50th parallel, with vineyards on a steep slope. It's one of the first estates planted entirely with Riesling, from 1720. A statue of the messenger, the Spätlesereiter, stands in its courtyard. Its wines use coloured capsules to mark quality levels.

steps.prompt: Which developed from the Spätlese tradition?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Spätlese was born at Schloss Johannisberg in 1775
Noble rot concentrated the late-picked grapes
Schloss Johannisberg was planted entirely with Riesling from 1720
